deficiencies.description: A meningioma is a type of tumour, not an anatomical site. The rewrite states 'when the tumour occurs in a meningioma or in the liver', distorting 'meningioma' into a location where a tumour occurs.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: Only 10% of these deaths, generally, if they're occurring in things like the meningioma that I was telling you about or in the liver.
deficiencies.rewritePassage: for example when the tumour occurs in a meningioma or in the liver.

deficiencies.description: The rewrite adds the linking word 'therefore', asserting a causal link between the small size of the niche and the tumour interfering with the bone marrow, which was not explicitly drawn by the lecturer.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: This niche is not very big. This will interfere with your bone marrow
deficiencies.rewritePassage: This niche is not very big. The tumour will therefore interfere with the bone marrow

considerations.sourcePassage: Things like obstruction of the bile ducts in the liver interferes with digestion.
considerations.reason: The sentence 'Other effects depend on the site' was added as a stylistic transition to introduce the subsequent site-dependent examples and does not introduce an unsupported factual claim.

considerations.sourcePassage: So you can see that there are lots of different ways in which the cancer can lead to illness and disease in people.
considerations.reason: The word 'therefore' in 'Cancer can therefore lead to illness and disease in many different ways' reflects the conclusion drawn by the lecturer's 'So you can see that'.

considerations.sourcePassage: erosion of that bone function, so you can get fractures
considerations.reason: Rewriting this as 'erosion of the bone, so that fractures can occur' conveys the same clinical meaning.

considerations.sourcePassage: Also ulceration, you saw that enormous cauliflower structure within the colon.
considerations.reason: Describing it as an 'enormous cauliflower-like structure seen within the colon' faithfully captures the lecturer's reference to gross tumour morphology while removing conversational filler.
